summary: Please is a flat hand circling on the chest. It's one of the first signs taught and one of the most used, both to ask politely and to say 'go ahead.'
steps: Place a flat hand, palm against your chest.
Circle it clockwise (from your point of view) two or three times.
Add a soft, slightly asking expression. PLEASE with a flat face reads as impatient.
note: PLEASE and SORRY are made in the same spot with the same circle. The difference is the handshape: a flat open hand for please, a fist for sorry. Learn them together so you never mix them up.
mistakes: Circling too big or too fast. Keep it small and smooth, like rubbing a spot on your shirt.

faq.q: Does PLEASE go at the start or end of a sentence?
faq.a: Usually at the end, or on its own. 'Water, please' is WATER PLEASE. You can also sign it alone with a questioning face to mean 'may I?'
